signals.text: We provide opportunities for all children to explore and share their thoughts, ideas and feelings through a variety of art, design, technology, music, drama, movement, dance and imaginative play activities.

Children have many different opportunities to develop their singing voice, learn how to play a variety of percussion instruments (untuned and tuned), learn basic music notation and experiment with composition of music.

Performing is a skill the children develop through assemblies, plays, concerts and this also includes opportunities for pupils to perform instruments they learn in school and also instruments they may learn at home; this helps to widen all children’s experience of Music.

Welcome to our school
St. John’s Catholic School is a one form entry Catholic Primary School that seeks to promote a distinctive contribution to every child’s education, by offering a warm and caring environment for all children in our school. The importance of the home and school partnership is central to our work here.
We aim to give every child the opportunity to achieve their full potential and our motto is “to love and serve one another.” We are a small, friendly school, with high expectations for all children.
Our school is in the heart of Rotherhithe and there are excellent transport links to Canada Water (our nearest tube station).

About us
About our school
We are located in a single-storey building set within pleasant grounds, including a secure astro-turf ball cage and a trim trail that children enjoy using during playtimes. We also have a dedicated planting area where children enthusiastically grow vegetables, fruit, and flowers. In addition, we are fortunate to be situated adjacent to Stave Hill Eco-Park, which we use as a valuable outdoor learning resource to enhance class-based activities.
The school has seven classes, one for each year group, with a maximum of 30 pupils per class. We also have a nursery offering both part-time and full-time places. The Nursery and Reception classes benefit from their own separate, well-equipped outdoor play areas.
The aim of St John’s is to provide a caring Christian environment in which the love of God is present and nurtured. We seek to support all members of our community in growing spiritually, while fostering an industrious and stimulating environment where every child’s potential can be fully developed.
St John’s is proud to be an outstanding school. Our most recent Ofsted inspection in 2024 judged all areas as outstanding, recognising the exceptionally high standards across the school. Inspectors highlighted pupils’ exemplary behaviour, the strength of our curriculum, and the wide range of enrichment opportunities, including educational visits, visitors, and specialist activities that enhance learning.
We are also delighted to have strong links with the Royal Academy of Music through the First Strings programme, giving children the opportunity to learn a string instrument from an early age and develop a lifelong appreciation of music.
Our extensive sporting provision further enriches pupils’ experiences and includes opportunities such as sailing, street dance, and golf, alongside a broad range of physical activities that promote teamwork, confidence, and wellbeing.
St John’s is part of a hard federation with St James the Great Primary School in Peckham.
Children’s Quotes:
I feel extremely safe in school because I know the adults are keeping us as safe as they can.
I enjoy Music because I love writing songs and we got to perform and it makes me proud
I enjoyed meeting the children from St. James School and making friends.
I love going to the woodlands, because we are seeing different birds and hearing birds sing

Welcome Back!
We were delighted to welcome all the children back after the holidays. We hope you all had peaceful Easter. This term, we are all excited for all the learning, playing and wonderful experiences this new term will bring. More details will follow in the coming weeks.
In the first of our Eastertide Assemblies, this week we learned that Thomas struggled to believe in Jesus’ Resurrection until he saw for himself. We are reminded that in Eastertide, we are invited to trust in Jesus and receive his blessings as we use our eyes if faith to believe.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to our school
St. John’s Catholic School is a one form entry Catholic Primary School that seeks to promote a distinctive contribution to every child’s education, by offering a warm and caring environment for all children in our school. The importance of the home and school partnership is central to our work here.
We aim to give every child the opportunity to achieve their full potential and our motto is “to love and serve one another.” We are a small, friendly school, with high expectations for all children.
Our school is in the heart of Rotherhithe and there are excellent transport links to Canada Water (our nearest tube station).

Nursery & Reception
Nursery & Reception
Welcome
We look forward to welcoming our new families to the Nursery Class at St. John’s Catholic School.
Day to day activities at Saint John’s School are planned around the 7 areas of Learning and Development.
Children are encouraged to develop the following 3 prime areas, first deemed most essential for healthy development and future learning: 1. Communication and language 2. Physical development 3. Personal, social and emotional development
As children grow, these 3 prime areas will help them to develop skills in the following 4 specific areas: 1. Literacy 2. Mathematics 3. Understanding the world 4. Expressive arts & design
In the foundation stage children have the opportunity to experience and investigate a range of materials and equipment both indoors and outside. Each child is encouraged to be independent and self-motivated in a safe and caring environment, which encourages each pupil to explore and be able to have confidence in his/her own judgements and ideas. We aim to promote learning as an enjoyable and challenging experience which children will continue to pursue for the rest of their lives.

Our Governors
Our Governors
The Federation of St James the Great and St John’s Catholic Primary Schools Governing Body Membership and Roles
Annual Governance Statement
The Governing Body is constituted is constituted by an Instrument of Government made by the Archdiocese of Southwark. The Instrument sets out the categories, numbers and terms of office of governors:
The governing body sets the strategic direction, the vision and the ethos of the school. In doing so it has a number of key responsibilities:
The governors carry out these functions through its termly full meetings, visits to the school and the work of its three principle committees:
Other committees are put together to deal with other functions including Pay Review Appeal (PRA), Complaints, Grievances, Pupil Discipline, Reorganisation as and when needed. Additionally there are named governors alongside an independent advisor for the Headteachers’ Performance and Salary Review committee (HTPSR).
Governors along with staff members who regularly attend meetings of the governing body and its committees must declare any business or personal interest that might influence any decision they may make especially in financial matters. Any governor with such an interest must declare it annually and notify the school of any changes that occur. Where there is a conflict of interest the governor must withdraw from the meeting and take no part in the discussions or vote. The agenda of each meeting requires governors and non-governors present to declare any interest they may have in any of the items to be discussed. Senior Leaders from both schools attend meetings as advisors The School Business Manager from St James the Great attends meeting and the Finance Officer for St John’s attends the Finance and Resources Committee meetings when required to do so.
9 Foundation Governors
2 Parent Governors (one from each school)
1 Executive Headteacher (ex-officio)
2 Co-opted Governors
recruit and performance manage the headteacher
exercise employer responsibility
ensure the school meets its statutory responsibilities
ensure financial probity
ensure the premises are well managed

Quorum:
The quorum for a full governing board meeting is one-half (rounded up to the nearest whole number) of the membership of the governing board, excluding any vacancies.
A quorum for committee meetings is determined by the committee, but must be made up of at least 3 governors who are members of that committee (see subsection 2). Associate members don’t count towards a quorum. PPC – quorum is stated as 3, S&C Quorum is 3 F&R is stated as 3.
There is delegated power to the F&R Committee to approve the budget.

Phonics
Teaching of phonics begins in the Nursery and continues throughout Reception and into Years 1 and 2 using the Collins ‘Song of Sounds’ programme. This teaches the letters in a specific sequence and in growing complexity, with words taught alongside the sounds. Children may progress quickly through each phase or may need extra support as they move through each of the phases.
Please take the time to have a look at their website and practice with your child.

Reading
Reading at St John’s is one of the most important things we can teach your child to do. Throughout the primary school journey, we teach pupils all the basic skills needed to enable them to read independently.
We want your child to love reading – and to want to read for enjoyment. This is why we work hard to make sure children develop a love of books as well as simply learning to read. We start by teaching phonics in Nursery using the highly successful ‘Song of Sounds’ phonics programme. Children learn how to ‘read’ the sounds in words and how those sounds can be written down. This is essential for reading, but it also helps children learn to spell well.
Once children can blend sounds together to read words, they practise reading books that match the phonics and the ‘tricky words’ they know. They start to believe they can read and this does wonders for their confidence. We ask that you help by listening to your child read every day.
